rows.subtype: Approach: notice the warning signs of pressure and isolation [Thinking]
rows.description: A student invited to a friendly self-improvement group sees that leaders discourage contact with family, demand large payments and label doubters as weak. Recognising these patterns creates distance.

rows.subtype: Approach: seek advice from a counsellor or former members [Action]
rows.description: The person reads accounts of ex-members and talks to a counsellor about the group's methods. Outside experience clarifies what is going on and reduces self-blame.

rows.subtype: Approach: commit gradually because each step seemed small [Pitfall]
rows.description: First a free workshop, then donations, then leaving college for group work. Each small step feels consistent with the last, and the escalation of commitment makes leaving harder.

rows.subtype: Approach: step away with support and a safe exit plan [Revision]
rows.description: Feeling uneasy, the person tells a trusted friend, avoids private meetings with leaders, and stops attending, leaning on family and, if threatened, the police. Leaving is planned with support.

rows.subtype: Approach: listing every task and estimating time [Thinking]
rows.description: A Class 5 child lists maths sums, a Hindi paragraph and a drawing, then guesses ten, twenty and thirty minutes each. Seeing the total is one hour helps her feel the work is finite and not scary.

rows.subtype: Approach: working in short blocks with small breaks [Action]
rows.description: A child sets a kitchen timer for twenty minutes of work and then five minutes of water and stretching. The breaks make the next block easier and the whole thing gets done before dinner.

rows.subtype: Approach: doing the easy fun parts first [Pitfall]
rows.description: A girl finishes the drawing and copying work first because they feel nice. By 8 pm only the hard sums remain, she is sleepy, and she rushes them with mistakes.

rows.subtype: Approach: seeing the crowded evening and redoing the plan [Revision]
rows.description: Halfway through, a boy notices a cousin is visiting at 6 pm. He moves the sums to before dinner, and does the reading after the guests leave, so nothing is left undone.

rows.subtopic: Responding to a natural disaster or accident
rows.subtype: Approach: safety first and quick triage [Thinking]
rows.description: When floodwater enters the street, a teen decides that people come before belongings, checks who is home, and moves grandparents and the younger sibling to the upper floor before anything else.

rows.subtopic: Responding to a natural disaster or accident
rows.subtype: Approach: basic first aid within trained limits [Action]
rows.description: A teen who completed a school first aid course applies pressure to a bleeding cut and keeps the injured person calm and still until adults or medical help arrive, and avoids moving someone with a possible neck injury.

rows.subtopic: Responding to a natural disaster or accident
rows.subtype: Approach: freezing or denying the danger [Pitfall]
rows.description: At the first tremor, a teen keeps scrolling her phone thinking it is nothing and loses precious seconds, since she had never rehearsed what to do and no action came to mind.

rows.subtopic: Responding to a natural disaster or accident
rows.subtype: Approach: adjusting when the plan meets reality [Revision]
rows.description: When the planned route is blocked by debris, a teen calmly takes an alternate way suggested by local volunteers, then updates the family group and the meeting point.

rows.subtype: Approach: looking at what is available before deciding [Thinking]
rows.description: A boy asked to make a school model finds cardboard, bottle caps, ice-cream sticks and old wire at home, and lets these materials suggest what he can build.

rows.subtype: Approach: drawing a sketch before cutting [Action]
rows.description: The girl draws a windmill on paper with measurements, so she can see what pieces she needs and avoid wasting the only sheet of thick cardboard.

rows.subtype: Approach: copying a video without adapting it [Pitfall]
rows.description: A boy follows an online tutorial needing items he does not have, so he ends up frustrated, and only when he replaces those parts with what is around does the model start to work.

rows.subtype: Approach: model collapses and is redesigned [Revision]
rows.description: When the tower of cardboard tubes falls over, the girl thinks the base is too narrow, widens it with a square frame and finds it now stands.

rows.subtopic: Planning a legacy or purpose project
rows.subtype: Approach: values-first exploration of purpose [Thinking]
rows.description: The person asks which problems keep drawing attention, such as rural education or clean water, and which of them fit their skills, before choosing a project to work on.

rows.subtopic: Planning a legacy or purpose project
rows.subtype: Approach: starting with a small pilot [Action]
rows.description: A software worker begins by teaching free weekend coding classes to twenty students in a nearby village school, learning what works before planning anything larger.

rows.subtopic: Planning a legacy or purpose project
rows.subtype: Approach: grand vision with no first step [Pitfall]
rows.description: The person dreams of transforming education across the state, spends months on presentations and logos, and never starts. The size of the dream makes any first action seem too small.

rows.subtopic: Planning a legacy or purpose project
rows.subtype: Approach: changing direction after evidence [Revision]
rows.description: After a year, data shows that the weekend classes reach few girls. The person adds a timing for mothers' approval and a women teacher, adapting the plan to evidence from the community.

rows.subtype: Approach: breaking cleaning his room into small jobs [Thinking]
rows.description: A boy is overwhelmed by a messy room. He splits it into clothes, books, toys and floor, and does one at a time, so the mess seems smaller with each finished part.

rows.subtype: Approach: putting everything on the bed then sorting it [Action]
rows.description: A girl picks up everything from the floor and puts it on the bed, then sorts into piles for cupboard, shelf and bin. Making a single pile shows what is there and makes choices easier.

rows.subtype: Approach: stuffing things under the bed to look clean [Pitfall]
rows.description: A child hides clutter under the bed to satisfy his mother quickly. The room looks neat but the next day he cannot find his school shoes, and the mess is still there.

rows.subtype: Approach: noticing a chore keeps piling up and finding why [Revision]
rows.description: A child sees his laundry basket is always overflowing. He realises he leaves clothes on the chair, so he puts the basket next to the chair and the problem gets smaller.
